title: To your Lord is the final end.
subtitle: Every road ends at the same place
then: Ibn Kathir says this is {idea}the return of everything on the Day of Resurrection{/idea}. Mu'adh bin Jabal stood among the tribe of Awd and said he was the Prophet's ﷺ envoy to them: {idea}know that the return is to Allah{/idea}, to Paradise or the Fire.
now: You map out a career path, a five-year plan, a retirement date. Every plan has a last line. {idea}This verse writes the true last line for all of them.{/idea}
old: My plans end where my life ends.
new: Every road I take ends with my Lord.
try: Look at one plan you are making and ask: how does this end with Allah?

title: He makes you laugh, and He makes you weep.
subtitle: Both your tears and your laughter come from Him
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}created in His creatures the ability to laugh or weep{/idea}, and the causes for each. Both opposites are His work. The listeners of Makkah are being shown a Lord who is present in their most ordinary moments.
now: Morning: a voice note from your child that makes you laugh out loud. Evening: a call from the hospital. {idea}Both moments come from the same Lord.{/idea} Neither is outside His care.
old: My good days are luck and my bad days are bad luck.
new: Both my laughter and my tears come from Him, so I can turn to Him in both.
try: The next time you laugh today, say Alhamdulillah. The next time you cry, say it too.

title: He causes death, and He gives life.
subtitle: The two doors only He opens
then: Ibn Kathir links this to another verse: {idea}He who created death and life{/idea}, to test which of you is best in deeds. The surah keeps listing what only Allah does, against the idols named earlier.
now: A maternity ward and an ICU on the same floor of the same hospital. You walk past both on the way to the lift. {idea}Every arrival and every departure there is His decision.{/idea}
old: Life and death are decided by medicine and luck.
new: Only He gives life and only He takes it, so my days are in His hand.
try: Visit or call someone who is ill today.

title: He created the pairs, male and female.
subtitle: Two kinds, both His design
then: Earlier the surah rejected the claim that angels were Allah's daughters. Now it states that {idea}He creates both male and female{/idea}. Ibn Kathir links it to another surah: was he not a drop, then a clot, then shaped, then made into two sexes?
now: You look at a scan on the screen, waiting to hear boy or girl. {idea}Neither choice is yours, and both are His creation.{/idea} The verse puts that moment back in His hands.
old: One kind of child is more of a blessing than the other.
new: Both male and female are His creation and His gift.
try: Thank Allah today, by name, for each child or sibling in your family.

title: From a tiny drop, a whole person.
subtitle: The humble beginning of everyone
then: Ibn Kathir cites the verse: {trap}does man think he will be left neglected?{/trap} Was he not a drop? Then a clot, then shaped. It ends: {idea}is He not able to give life to the dead?{/idea} The beginning argues for the return.
now: You hold a newborn in the hospital and cannot believe something this whole began so small. {idea}The same power is behind the promise of resurrection.{/idea} Your start is proof of your return.
old: Resurrection is too hard to believe.
new: If He made me from a drop, bringing me back is not hard for Him.
try: Look at your own hand for ten seconds and remember it began as a drop.

title: Upon Him is the second creation.
subtitle: He made you once. He will make you again.
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}just as He first originated creation, He is able to bring it back{/idea}, resurrecting it for the Day of Judgement. The answer to doubt about the return is the first creation itself.
now: You rebuild an app you once wrote and it takes a fraction of the time, because you made it before. {idea}Remaking is never harder for the one who made it.{/idea}
old: Once I am dust, that is the end of me.
new: The One who made me once has promised to make me again.
try: Say tonight before sleep: in Your name I die and I live.

title: He gives wealth, and He gives contentment.
subtitle: Two gifts: having, and being satisfied
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah gives wealth and lets it remain, so people can benefit from it. Mujahid said aghna is {reward}He gives wealth{/reward}. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid also said aqna means {reward}He gave contentment{/reward}.
now: Payday arrives, and two days later you feel just as short as before. Someone else earns half and sleeps fine. {reward}Wealth and contentment are two different gifts, and both are His.{/reward}
old: If I earn more, I will finally feel enough.
new: Wealth and contentment are separate gifts. I can ask for both.
try: In your dua today, ask Allah for contentment with what you have, by name.

title: He is the Lord of Sirius.
subtitle: The star they worshipped has a Lord
then: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said ash-Shi'ra is {idea}the bright star, Sirius{/idea}, which {trap}a group of Arabs used to worship{/trap}. The surah names it to say: even the brightest thing in your sky has a Lord.
now: A celebrity, a bright career, a big name on a stage. Some things shine so hard that people start treating them as more than human. {idea}Brightness is still created.{/idea} It has a Lord.
old: Some people and things are so impressive they deserve awe.
new: Even the brightest thing has a Lord. The awe belongs to Him.
try: When someone dazzles you today, say quietly: their Lord is greater.

title: He destroyed the former people of Ad.
subtitle: The strongest nation, gone
then: Ad were the people of Hud. Ibn Kathir says they were {trap}among the strongest and fiercest people{/trap}, and the most rebellious against Allah and His messenger. He links it to Iram of the pillars, and the wind sent on them for seven nights and eight days.
now: You feel safe because of what you have built: the job title, the savings, the strong body at the gym. {idea}Strength is a gift, not a shield against Allah.{/idea} Use it for Him.
old: If I am strong and secure enough, nothing can touch me.
new: Strength did not save Ad. Only turning to Allah keeps me safe.
try: Use one of your strengths today to help someone weaker.

title: And Thamud, none of them left.
subtitle: A whole people, no remnant
then: Ibn Kathir says this {trap}declares that He destroyed them all and spared none{/trap}. The surah lists the ruined peoples one after another, so the warning builds.
now: You read about a company that collapsed overnight, every job gone. You assume you would have seen it coming. {idea}The verse asks: what are you ignoring right now?{/idea}
old: Stories of ruined nations are history, not a message to me.
new: These stories are warnings for how I live today.
try: Name one warning sign in your own life you keep ignoring, and take one step about it.

title: Nuh's people before them were worse still.
subtitle: The longest warning, the hardest refusal
then: The people of Nuh came {idea}before Ad and Thamud{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says they were {trap}more unjust in disobeying Allah than those who came after them{/trap}. The surah moves backward through history to its first great refusal.
now: Someone keeps reminding you, kindly, for years: pray, call your mother, stop that habit. The longer you refuse, the easier refusing gets. {trap}Long refusal hardens.{/trap}
old: I have heard this reminder a hundred times. It does not move me now.
new: A long refusal is more serious, not less. I can still turn back.
try: Take one reminder you keep brushing off and act on it today.
